experiment: Trip 5c: the capture engine's AUDIO code path (no EDC, no data-sector layout check), 1024 sectors at FAD 63000; two runs.

hardware.disc: Sword of the Berserk (TOC: T01 data 150-1076, T02 audio 1076-1602, T03 data 45150-549300)

important: FAD 63000 is inside track 3, which on this disc is a DATA track. So this measured the audio code path on data sectors: the timings are real and isolate the EDC cost, but it says nothing about how fast a real audio track reads. The bench now warns about exactly this (kui_bench_fad_note).

conclusions: The audio path skips EDC and is +2.5% faster than the data path at crc32/no-read-back (722.5 against 704.9 KiB/s), which matches the 2.8% EDC share Trip 5a measured. Every parts line shows edc=0 ms.
With SHA-256 on, the difference disappears (-0.0% and -0.4%): SHA-256 dominates, so removing EDC changes little.
What this does NOT answer: the read rate of real audio tracks. On this disc the only audio track is 526 sectors in the low-density area; an audio-heavy disc (MDK2, 29 audio tracks) is still untested.

limitations: Measured on data sectors read through the audio code path, not on an audio track.
One card, one disc, one console; two runs; 1024 sectors per point.
